title: Phase out mono CLI in favor of devenv tasks
description:
## Goal

Migrate from custom `mono` CLI commands to native devenv tasks, following the pattern already established in effect-utils.

## Current State in effect-utils

effect-utils has already migrated most mono commands to devenv tasks (see `scripts/mono.ts`):

```
# Old mono commands → New devenv tasks
mono bun install    → dt bun:install
mono genie          → dt genie:run / genie:watch / genie:check
mono ts             → dt ts:check / ts:watch / ts:build / ts:clean
mono lint           → dt lint:check / lint:fix
mono test           → dt test:run / test:watch / test:unit / test:integration
mono check          → dt check:quick / check:all
```

Only `mono nix` and `mono context` remain as CLI commands.

## Why Migrate

### Benefits of devenv tasks over mono CLI:

1. **Native tooling** - `devenv tasks list`, `dt <task>`
2. **Dependency ordering** - `after = ["deps"]` built-in
3. **Idempotency** - `status` checks skip unnecessary work
4. **Automatic execution** - `before = ["devenv:enterShell"]`
5. **No custom CLI maintenance** - less code to maintain
6. **Discoverable** - `devenv tasks list` shows all available tasks
7. **Composable** - tasks can depend on each other

### What mono CLI still provides:

* `mono nix status/rebuild` - CLI staleness checking
* `mono context` - workspace context info
* Complex orchestration that doesn't fit task model

## Migration Plan

### Phase 1: Audit mono commands across repos

- [ ] List all mono subcommands in livestore
- [ ] List all mono subcommands in other repos
- [ ] Identify which map cleanly to devenv tasks

### Phase 2: Create devenv task equivalents

For each command, create task with:

```nix
tasks."category:action" = {
  exec = "...";
  status = "...";  # Optional: skip if already done
  after = [...];   # Optional: dependencies
};
```

### Phase 3: Deprecate mono commands

* Add deprecation warnings pointing to devenv tasks
* Update documentation
* Eventually remove from mono CLI

## Task Naming Convention (from effect-utils)

```
bun:install
genie:run | genie:watch | genie:check
ts:check | ts:watch | ts:build | ts:clean  
lint:check | lint:fix
test:run | test:watch | test:unit | test:integration
check:quick | check:all
```

## Related Issues

* oep-6nt: Automatic repo setup via devenv tasks (uses same pattern)

## Files

* `effect-utils/scripts/mono.ts` - reference implementation
* `effect-utils/devenv.nix` - task definitions
* `livestore/devenv.nix` - needs task migration

title: Upstream: extract otel-span as standalone Nix package
description:
otel-span is currently inline in the OTEL devenv module (nix/devenv-modules/otel.nix). Extract it as a standalone derivation so projects can add it to devenv packages without importing the full OTEL module (which starts local collector/tempo/grafana processes).

This is needed because livestore wants to use the global system OTEL stack, not a local one, but still needs otel-span for dt task tracing.

Acceptance criteria:
- otel-span available as effectUtils.packages.${system}.otel-span (or similar)
- Can be added to devenv packages list independently

title: Upstream: enhance makeOtelCliLayer with root span, bootstrap timing, Grafana URL
description:
effect-utils' makeOtelCliLayer is lighter than livestore's OtelLiveHttp (uses @effect/opentelemetry/Otlp, no SDK peer deps) but lacks:

1. Root span creation (Layer.span with configurable name/attributes)
2. Node.js bootstrap timing instrumentation
3. Grafana trace URL logging (onEnd callback)
4. Metrics reader setup

Enhance makeOtelCliLayer to support these features so livestore can switch to it and drop the heavy @opentelemetry/sdk-* dependencies.

See livestore's OtelLiveHttp in packages/@livestore/utils-dev/src/node/mod.ts for reference.

title: Prefer patched tsc without build-time Effect diagnostics
description:
## Context

We currently run unpatched Nix tsc for dt ts:build / dt ts:check to avoid Effect language-service diagnostics (TS28/TS41/TS44 etc) failing CLI builds.

This keeps full TypeScript build/typechecking but defers build-time Effect diagnostics enforcement.

## Goal

Switch back to patched tsc for build-time parity while keeping Effect diagnostics IDE-only (or at least non-fatal in CLI builds).

## Approach

- Update @effect/language-service plugin options in generated tsconfigs to stop emitting diagnostics in patched tsc (e.g. includeSuggestionsInTsc: false and downgrade warning severities to suggestion/message, or selectively turn off specific diagnostics).
- Ensure IDE diagnostics remain available.

## Acceptance

- dt ts:build uses patched tsc
- dt ts:build passes without large code churn
- Effect diagnostics remain visible in IDE

Validation: `devenv shell dt ts:check --no-tui`, `devenv shell dt ts:build --no-tui`.`

title: Import effect directly from effect/@effect packages and deduplicate utils
description:
type: task

## Goal

Align livestore with the effect-utils pattern for effect imports:

1. **Import effect directly**: Replace re-exports through @livestore/utils/effect with direct imports from effect, @effect/platform, @effect/rpc, etc.
2. **Shrink effect-utils barrel**: The effect-utils package should only export what it actually defines (custom utilities, helpers), not re-export upstream effect packages.
3. **Prune @livestore/utils**: Remove definitions from @livestore/utils that are already provided by effect-utils, improving code reuse across the megarepo.

## Context

Currently @livestore/utils/effect re-exports many things from effect and @effect/* packages. This creates unnecessary indirection and makes it harder to see what's actually custom vs upstream. effect-utils already follows the pattern of direct imports — livestore should match.

Auto-generate AGENTS.md via genie
description:
## Problem

[AGENTS.md](<http://AGENTS.md>) files need to be manually maintained across packages. They often become stale or inconsistent with actual package capabilities.

## Current State

* [AGENTS.md](<http://AGENTS.md>) files exist in some packages but not all
* Content is manually written and may drift from reality
* No automated generation or validation

## Open Questions

* What should be auto-generated vs manually curated?
* Should it pull from package.json, README, or code analysis?
* How to handle package-specific vs workspace-wide info?

## Possible Directions

1. **Template-based**: Genie generates from .genie.ts metadata
2. **Code analysis**: Extract exports, commands, types automatically
3. **Hybrid**: Auto-generate structure, allow manual sections
4. **Validation only**: Lint existing [AGENTS.md](<http://AGENTS.md>) for staleness

## Notes

Keep this issue open for further exploration. The right approach depends on:

* How much structure [AGENTS.md](<http://AGENTS.md>) should have
* Whether LLMs benefit more from generated or curated content
* Integration with existing genie workflow

title: Improve binary version checking discoverability in mono
description:
## Problem

The `mono nix status` command exists to check binary staleness, but it's not discoverable and users don't know when their CLIs need rebuilding.

## Current State

* `mono nix status` checks if built CLIs match current source
* Uses `cli-build-stamp.nix` to compare git hashes
* No proactive warnings when binaries are stale
* Documentation is scattered across multiple locations

## Technical Details

The staleness check works by:

1. Recording git commit hash at build time in a stamp file
2. Comparing stamp to current HEAD on status check
3. Reporting which CLIs are out of date

Current invocation:

```bash
mono nix status  # Manual check, no auto-trigger
```

## Proposed Solution

Add proactive staleness warnings:

1. **Shell hook approach**: Check on devenv entry

```nix
enterShell = ''
  if ! mono nix status --quiet; then
    echo "⚠️  Some CLIs are stale. Run 'mono nix rebuild' to update."
  fi
'';
```

2. **CLI integration**: Add `--check-stale` to mono commands
3. **Help text**: Add `mono nix` to `mono --help` output prominently

## Files to Modify

* `packages/@anthropic/mono-cli/src/commands/nix.ts` (add --quiet flag)
* `devenv.nix` (add shell hook)
* `README.md` or `AGENTS.md` (document workflow)

title: Add worktree support to dotdot
description:
## Problem

Dotdot lacks support for git worktrees, making it difficult to work on multiple branches simultaneously in a megarepo setup.

## Current State

* PR #63 (effect-utils) adds some worktree infrastructure to megarepo
* The `isolate` and `unisolate` commands are NOT yet implemented
* Basic worktree listing may exist but full workflow support is missing

## Technical Details

Git worktrees allow checking out multiple branches simultaneously:

```bash
git worktree add ../feature-branch feature-branch
# Work in ../feature-branch while main stays in original dir
```

For megarepos, worktrees need special handling:

1. Shared node_modules strategies (symlinks vs separate installs)
2. Build artifact isolation
3. Config file handling (some should be shared, some isolated)

## Proposed Solution

1. Implement `dotdot worktree add <branch>` command
2. Add `dotdot worktree list` to show active worktrees
3. Handle node_modules: option for shared (symlink) or isolated
4. Integrate with existing dotdot workspace detection

## Related Issues

* oep-ejolnc: Package conflicts with worktrees (dependency)

title: mr sync doesn't update megarepo root's flake.lock
description:
mr sync updates megarepo.lock correctly, but the Nix lock sync feature only processes flake.lock files inside member directories (e.g., repos/effect-utils/), not the megarepo root's own flake.lock.

When effect-utils is updated and pushed, running 'mr sync' in dotfiles updates megarepo.lock to the new commit, but flake.lock still points to the old GitHub revision. Users must manually run 'nix flake lock --update-input effect-utils' to update.

The nix-lock sync code (nix-lock/mod.ts) iterates over members and looks for flake.lock inside member directories, but the megarepo root's flake.lock is outside this scope.

title: dt nix:hash fails to auto-fix when pnpm offline install fails
description:
dt nix:hash:megarepo (and similar tasks) fail to automatically update the hash when the pnpm lockfile has changed but the hash itself hasn't triggered a mismatch.

The task looks for 'got: sha256-...' hash mismatch errors in the build output. But when the pnpmDepsHash points to a valid (but outdated) store, pnpm fails with ERR_PNPM_NO_OFFLINE_TARBALL instead of a hash mismatch.

Error seen:
  ERR_PNPM_NO_OFFLINE_TARBALL  A package is missing from the store but cannot download it in offline mode.

The task reports: 'build failed but no hash mismatch found' and gives up.

Workaround: Manually set a fake hash (sha256-AAA...) to force a hash mismatch, which reveals the correct hash.

Suggested fix: Detect ERR_PNPM_NO_OFFLINE_TARBALL errors and automatically try the fake-hash trick, or add a --force flag.

title: Enable remaining type-aware oxlint rules
description:
We enabled type-aware linting with oxlint to catch @deprecated usage via the typescript/no-deprecated rule.

However, to avoid a large initial cleanup, we disabled the other type-aware rules with TODO comments in genie/oxlint-base.ts. These should be re-enabled incrementally:

Rules to enable (by occurrence count):
- typescript/no-unsafe-type-assertion (325) - warns about unsafe type assertions
- typescript/no-unnecessary-type-arguments (54) - detects unnecessary type arguments
- typescript/no-unnecessary-type-assertion (48) - detects unnecessary type assertions
- typescript/no-unnecessary-boolean-literal-compare (46) - detects unnecessary boolean comparisons
- typescript/no-misused-spread (18) - detects misused spread operators
- typescript/no-redundant-type-constituents (12) - detects redundant type constituents
- typescript/no-floating-promises (9) - detects floating promises
- typescript/no-base-to-string (6) - detects improper toString usage
- typescript/no-unsafe-enum-comparison (5) - detects unsafe enum comparisons
- typescript/unbound-method (4) - detects unbound methods
- typescript/restrict-template-expressions (3) - restricts template expression types
- typescript/no-duplicate-type-constituents (3) - detects duplicate type constituents
- typescript/no-unsafe-unary-minus (1) - detects unsafe unary minus
- typescript/no-unnecessary-template-expression (1) - detects unnecessary template expressions

Approach:
1. Pick a rule with low occurrence count
2. Enable it in genie/oxlint-base.ts
3. Run dt genie:run && dt lint:check
4. Fix the violations
5. Repeat

Files:
- genie/oxlint-base.ts - Rule configuration
- nix/devenv-modules/tasks/shared/lint-oxc.nix - Type-aware lint task config
- devenv.nix - tsconfig and tsgolint package config

title: Investigate and fix TypeScript composite build ordering issue causing spurious DOM errors
description:
In composite tsc --build tsconfig.dev.json, Group 1/2 TS errors (globalThis/window/document not found) appear during clean full builds but NOT when building individual packages. All affected packages have lib: [ES2024, DOM, DOM.Iterable] via domLib, yet the composite build acts as if DOM types are missing.

Key observations:
- tsc --build packages/@livestore/livestore/tsconfig.json (individual) -> 0 errors
- tsc --build tsconfig.dev.json (composite, clean) -> 14 errors (Groups 1/2)
- Building one package first, then incremental full build -> 0 Group 1/2 errors
- Likely a TypeScript composite build ordering quirk where files get type-checked before their project lib declarations are fully resolved

Currently suppressed with @ts-ignore comments (oep-zsl.5, commit 57ed42997). P1 to investigate and properly fix after genie-igor-ci branch merges.

Affected files: devtools.ts, StoreRegistry.ts, dev.ts, sync-electric/index.ts, sync-s2/sync-provider.ts
Related: oep-8tc (P3, broader DOM type declarations task)

Group 2 - Missing window/document types (TS2304/TS2584, 4 errors):
- StoreRegistry.ts: typeof window
- dev.ts: window.URL, document.createElement
These are browser-only utility files that need DOM types but the package tsconfig deliberately excludes 'dom' lib.

Group 3 - TS2742 inferred type not portable (5 errors):

title: Consider improving otel CLI usability for scripting and agent use
description:
Feedback from a coding agent session revealed friction when using the otel CLI programmatically. Three areas to consider:

1. **Startup overhead / output noise** — Every otel command goes through direnv exec which runs devenv tasks, adding ~15s of noise to stdout. Makes CLI output unpipeable, forcing fallback to raw curl.

2. **Filtering support** — otel api outputs pretty JSON but has no built-in filtering. A --jq flag or pipe-friendly mode would help.

3. **Dashboard inspection** — No way to inspect dashboard config without raw API. Something like otel dashboard inspect <uid> could help.

These are considerations, not immediate action items. Workaround: curl + jq.

title: Consider suppressing devenv task output in otel CLI commands
description: Every otel command goes through direnv exec which runs devenv tasks, adding ~15s of noise to stdout. This makes the CLI output unpipeable and forces users to fall back to raw curl. Consider detecting non-interactive / piped mode and suppressing task runner output.

title: Consider adding --jq flag or pipe-friendly output mode to otel api
description: otel api outputs pretty-printed JSON but has no built-in filtering. A --jq flag (e.g. otel api grafana GET /api/health --jq '.database') or a --raw mode for cleaner piping would make the CLI more useful for scripting and agent use.

title: Consider adding otel dashboard inspect command
description: There's no way to inspect dashboard config (panels, variables, queries) without going through the raw Grafana API. Something like 'otel dashboard inspect <uid>' could surface panel config, templating variables, etc. in a structured way.

title: OTel devenv tracing tooling improvements
description: Shell entry profiling revealed that current tracing setup has significant gaps that prevent end-to-end visibility into devenv shell startup performance. Warm shell entry takes ~2.7-5.3s with a 500ms target (R10). We need better tooling to diagnose and optimize this.
notes: All 6 sub-tasks implemented in commit e998ab5. Key change: otlpjsonfilereceiver replaces curl for span delivery.

title: Add root span for shell entry (devenv:enterShell)
description: Shell entry goes through devenv directly, not through the dt wrapper, so no root trace span is created. Individual tasks emit orphan spans via trace.status. We need a root span wrapping the entire enterShell lifecycle so child task spans can be correlated into a single trace. This would enable end-to-end waterfall visualization.
notes: Implemented: setup:gate generates root TRACEPARENT, setup:save-hash emits devenv:shell:entry root span. Commit e998ab5.

title: Enable end-to-end waterfall view for shell startup
description: Currently there is no way to see a waterfall/timeline view of the entire shell startup sequence. Task spans are emitted as orphans without a shared trace context. Need to propagate TRACEPARENT from the root enterShell span to all child task executions so Grafana/Tempo can render a proper waterfall showing sequential vs parallel task execution.
notes: Implemented: TRACEPARENT propagation at 3 layers (setup:gate → trace.nix fallback → dt wrapper). Enables waterfall view in Grafana Tempo. Commit e998ab5.

title: Add visibility into Nix evaluation phase
description: Nix evaluation (direnv + nix eval) takes ~1.1s on warm entry but is completely invisible to our tracing. This phase happens before any shell code runs, so otel-span cannot instrument it. Need to either: (a) wrap the direnv/nix eval in a span from outside, (b) use nix eval hooks/timestamps, or (c) infer it as dead time between shell invocation and first task span.
notes: Implemented: SHELL_ENTRY_TIME_NS captured at enterShell, shell.ready_ms attribute added to dt spans, shell:ready marker span emitted. Commit e998ab5.

title: Surface dead time between task executions
description: There are gaps between task executions during shell startup that are not visible in traces. These gaps include devenv scheduler overhead, status check dispatch, and inter-task coordination. Without visibility into dead time, we cannot identify whether bottlenecks are in tasks themselves or in the orchestration between them.
notes: Implemented via waterfall tracing: root span + child task spans in same trace enable dead time visibility in Grafana Tempo trace viewer. No separate instrumentation needed. Commit e998ab5.

title: Reduce otel-span tracing overhead (currently 19% of shell startup)
description: otel-span adds ~58ms per invocation. With 14+ sequential cached task status checks during warm shell entry, tracing itself adds ~470ms — 19% of total startup time, exceeding the R10h budget of <10%. Options: (a) batch spans instead of per-task otel-span invocations, (b) use a long-lived OTLP exporter process, (c) async/fire-and-forget span emission, (d) reduce number of traced status checks.
notes: Implemented: Replaced curl POST with file append to spool dir (otlpjsonfilereceiver). Per-span overhead reduced from ~58ms to <1ms. Status check tracing removed. Commit e998ab5.

title: Track devshell re-evaluation frequency via OTel metrics
description: We have no visibility into how often the devshell gets re-evaluated (cold starts triggered by direnv detecting input changes). This matters for understanding developer experience — frequent re-evals mean frequent ~50s cold starts. Options: (a) emit a counter metric from enterShell distinguishing cold vs warm (e.g. based on whether setup:gate status passes), (b) emit a span with shell.cold=true/false attribute, (c) track via direnv hook that detects Nix re-eval. This would help answer: how often do devs hit cold starts, and what triggers them.
notes: Implemented: Cold-start detection via cold_start attribute on shell:ready span. Checks .direnv/task-cache/setup-git-hash existence and git hash match. Commit e998ab5.

title: Upgrade oxfmt to fix sort_imports crash on docs/.netlify build artifacts
description:
## Problem

oxfmt 0.23.0 (current Nix version) crashes with a panic in the sort_imports transform when processing files containing template literals with `/*` inside them. This affects Netlify build artifacts in `docs/.netlify/` which contain bundled Astro SSR output with embedded code snippets.

The crash causes `dt lint:check:format` to fail silently (exit code from crash), making the pre-commit hook (`check:quick`) unreliable.

## Root Cause

Known upstream bug: [oxc-project/oxc#17788](https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc/issues/17788)
- The sort_imports IR transform misidentifies `/*` inside template literals as alignable comments
- Minimal reproduction: a file containing `\`/*\`` (template literal with `/*`)
- Fix PR: [oxc-project/oxc#17791](https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc/pull/17791)
- Fixed in oxfmt v0.24.0 (released 2026-01-12)

## Fix

Two changes needed:
1. **Upgrade oxfmt** from 0.23.0 to >= 0.24.0 (ideally latest 0.31.0) in the Nix package/flake
2. **Add `.netlify` to `.oxfmtrc.json` ignorePatterns** — these are build artifacts that should never be formatted regardless. Pattern: `**/.netlify/**`

Note: The root `.gitignore` already contains `.netlify` but oxfmt does not correctly resolve this pattern for nested paths like `docs/.netlify/`.

title: Handle package conflicts with worktrees
description:
## Problem

When using git worktrees in a megarepo, package version conflicts can arise between the main checkout and worktree checkouts.

## Current State

* No conflict detection exists for worktree scenarios
* Each worktree may have different dependency versions
* Shared node_modules can cause subtle runtime errors

## Technical Details

Conflict scenarios:

1. Main has `lodash@4.17.21`, worktree branch has `lodash@4.17.20`
2. Shared node_modules uses whichever was installed last
3. Type definitions may mismatch at build time
4. Runtime behavior differs from expected

## Proposed Solution

1. Add `dotdot worktree check` to detect version conflicts
2. Compare package.json/bun.lock across worktrees
3. Warn when shared dependencies have version mismatches
4. Suggest isolation strategy when conflicts detected

## Implementation Notes

* Parse bun.lock from each worktree
* Build dependency version map per worktree
* Diff maps to find conflicts
* Consider lock file hash comparison for quick check

## Depends On

* oep-2r6jc7: Basic worktree support must exist first

title: Refactor genie relative path handling
description:
## Problem

Genie's relative path handling is CWD-dependent and uses hardcoded assumptions, leading to inconsistent behavior when run from different directories.

## Current State

* Location semantics depend on current working directory
* Hardcoded `file:packages/` prefix in dependency resolution
* `computeRelativePath` function is duplicated across generators
* Path computation differs between package.json and tsconfig generators

## Technical Details

Example of CWD-dependency:

```typescript
// In packages/@overeng/genie/src/generators/package-json.ts
const relativePath = computeRelativePath(fromPackage, toPackage);
// Returns different results based on process.cwd()
```

Hardcoded prefix issue:

```typescript
// Assumes all packages are in packages/ directory
const depPath = `file:packages/${depName}`;
// Breaks for packages in other locations (e.g., apps/, tools/)
```

## Proposed Solution

1. **Centralize path computation**: Single `PathResolver` class
2. **Remove CWD dependency**: Use config file location as anchor
3. **Dynamic prefix**: Derive from actual package locations, not hardcoded
4. **Add tests**: Cover various directory structures

## Files to Modify

* `packages/@overeng/genie/src/utils/path-resolver.ts` (new)
* `packages/@overeng/genie/src/generators/package-json.ts`
* `packages/@overeng/genie/src/generators/tsconfig.ts`
* Add integration tests with different CWDs

title: Add devenv/direnv local fish autocomplete loading
description:
## Problem

Fish autocompletions for workspace-local CLIs (mono, genie, dotdot) aren't loaded when entering a devenv shell. Users must manually source completions.

## Current State

* CLIs support `--completions fish` but output isn't auto-loaded
* devenv's `enterShell` could generate and source completions
* No existing pattern for devenv-integrated completion loading

## Technical Details

Fish loads completions from:

1. `~/.config/fish/completions/` (user-global)
2. `/nix/store/.../share/fish/vendor_completions.d/` (nix packages)
3. Dynamically via `source` in shell init

For devenv, completions should be:

* Generated on shell entry (to match current CLI version)
* Sourced automatically without user action
* Isolated per-project (don't pollute global completions)

## Proposed Solution

Create a `fish-completion-sync` devenv plugin:

```nix
# In devenv.nix
enterShell = ''
  # Generate completions for workspace CLIs
  mono --completions fish | source
  genie --completions fish | source
  dotdot --completions fish | source
'';
```

Or create a reusable module:

```nix
imports = [ inputs.effect-utils.devenvModules.fish-completions ];
fish-completions.commands = [ "mono" "genie" "dotdot" ];
```

## Files to Create

* `nix/devenv-modules/fish-completions.nix`
* Update effect-utils flake to export module

Reduce otel CLI startup overhead (~15s direnv/devenv latency)
description:
Every `otel` CLI command invocation through `direnv exec` triggers the full devenv task runner, adding ~15s of overhead before the actual command runs. This makes the CLI impractical for interactive/scripting use — agents and users fall back to raw `curl` which is instant.

Root cause: `otel` is a TS CLI that runs via `bun` through a shell wrapper in the devenv profile. When invoked via `direnv exec . otel ...`, direnv re-evaluates the shell environment which triggers all setup tasks (pnpm:install, genie:run, megarepo:sync, ts:build, etc.) even when they're all cached.

Possible approaches:
1. **Pre-built binary** — Ship otel CLI as a Nix-built binary (like genie/megarepo) so it doesn't need the devenv shell at all
2. **Skip devenv tasks for CLI invocations** — Detect when running a one-shot CLI command vs entering the shell, and skip optional setup tasks
3. **Lazy direnv** — Only run direnv for env vars (OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, OTEL_GRAFANA_URL) without triggering the full task runner
4. **Direct invocation** — Allow `otel` to read config from a dotfile or env directly, bypassing direnv entirely

Impact: This overhead is the #1 reason the otel CLI gets bypassed in favor of curl during development and agent sessions.

comments.author: Johannes Schickling
comments.text:
## Investigation Results (2026-02-07)

### Measurements

| Scenario | Time | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| curl (baseline) | ~6ms | Direct HTTP, no overhead |
| otel health direct (bypass direnv) | ~360ms | Bun + TS module loading |
| Bun startup alone | ~8ms | Bun is fast; TS module load is ~350ms |
| direnv exec . true (warm cache) | ~875ms | direnv env setup + cached task checks |
| direnv exec . otel health (warm) | ~1.2s | direnv (~875ms) + otel (~360ms) |
| direnv exec . true (cold, no task cache) | ~13-21s | Full task execution (ts:build dominates) |

### Where time goes (cold start breakdown from traces)

Cold start runs devenv:enterShell which depends on setup:opt:* tasks:
- setup:opt:ts:build: ~13s (the dominator — runs tsc --build)
- pnpm:install:* chain: ~6s total (sequential, ~400-600ms each x ~15 packages)
- setup:opt:genie:run: ~1.5s
- setup:opt:megarepo:sync: ~0.5s

### OTEL observability gap

The cold-start overhead is invisible to dt traces. direnv runs devenv-tasks first (cold path), warming all caches. By the time dt runs, everything is cached (~680ms). The cold-start tasks emit orphan spans (no TRACEPARENT) which DO show up in Tempo with task.cached=false.

### Key insight: bimodal distribution

The overhead is NOT consistent:
- Warm (typical): ~1.2s — acceptable for interactive use, 200x slower than curl
- Cold (after cache clear/rebuild): ~13-21s — creates the perception of slowness

Cold starts happen after: direnv reload, clearing .direnv/task-cache, or switching branches.

comments.author: Johannes Schickling
comments.text:
## Root Cause Analysis (updated 2026-02-08)

### Why `direnv exec .` is needed
It's NOT actually needed. It's an artifact of running from a non-direnv shell (e.g. this bash tool, CI, etc.). In an interactive terminal where direnv has already loaded the env, you just run `otel health` directly — which takes ~360ms.

The `direnv exec` path is only needed when:
- Running from a tool/shell that hasn't loaded the direnv env
- CI environments
- Scripts that need to be self-contained

### Where the ~900ms warm overhead actually goes

The devenv `print-dev-env` output (cached in `.devenv/shell-*.sh`) contains a hardcoded call to:
```
devenv-tasks run devenv:enterShell --mode all
```

This runs on EVERY `direnv exec` call, even when all tasks are cached. It:
1. Starts the devenv-tasks binary (~50ms)
2. Loads and parses the task graph from tasks.json
3. Runs ~30 task status checks sequentially (each ~1ms but fork/exec adds up)
4. The entire enterShell tree executes: setup:gate, setup:opt:*, pnpm:install:*, megarepo:sync, beads:daemon:ensure, devenv:files, git-hooks, etc.

### Corrected latency breakdown

| Component | Time | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| direnv env cache lookup | ~20ms | Checks if watched files changed |
| Shell script `eval` (env vars) | ~30ms | Sources the cached shell-*.sh |
| `devenv-tasks run devenv:enterShell` | ~800ms | The dominator — runs on every exec |
| Actual command (e.g. `otel health`) | ~360ms | Bun + TS module load + HTTP calls |

### Implication
The ~900ms overhead is inherent to how devenv hooks into the shell. It's not a bug — it's ensuring the dev environment is always consistent. But for CLI tools like `otel` that just need env vars, it's unnecessary work.

Fix patches feature propagation in genie
description:
## Problem

Genie's patches feature doesn't propagate through the dependency graph like `peerDependencies` does. When a package defines patches, consuming packages don't automatically inherit them.

## Current State

* `peerDependencies` correctly propagates via `meta.data.peerDependencies` in generated configs
* `patches` are defined in `.genie.ts` but only applied to the defining package
* No `.data.patches` export pattern exists for propagation

## Technical Details

In genie configs:

```typescript
// Package A defines patches
export const config = definePackage({
  patches: { 'some-dep': './patches/fix.patch' }
})

// Package B depends on A but doesn't get A's patches
export const config = definePackage({
  dependencies: ['@scope/package-a']
})
```

## Proposed Solution

Implement patch propagation similar to peerDependencies:

1. Add `.data.patches` export to generated configs
2. Collect patches from transitive dependencies during generation
3. Merge patches with conflict detection (same dep, different patches)
4. Apply merged patches in consuming package's config

## Files to Modify

* `packages/@overeng/genie/src/generators/package-json.ts`
* `packages/@overeng/genie/src/types.ts` (add patches to metadata)
* Add tests for patch propagation scenarios

title: Add bun.lock freshness check to mono check
description:
## Problem

The `bun.lock` file can become stale when local `file:` dependencies are modified but `bun install` isn't re-run. This causes silent build failures and confusing errors.

## Current State

* A bash-based staleness check exists in `dotfiles/nixpkgs/home-manager/modules/direnv-stale-check/`
* It uses git commit ancestry (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`) to detect if dependencies changed
* The check runs via direnv shell hook, not integrated into `mono check`

## Technical Details

The check works by:

1. Parsing `bun.lock` JSONL format for `file:` dependencies with commit hashes
2. For each local dep, verifying if the recorded commit is an ancestor of current HEAD
3. Warning if any dependency's commit is not in the current history

## Proposed Solution

Port the staleness check to TypeScript as an Effect-based task in `mono check`:

1. Create `packages/@anthropic/mono-cli/src/tasks/bun-lock-freshness.ts`
2. Implement as `Effect.gen` task matching existing task patterns
3. Parse bun.lock, extract file: deps, run git ancestry checks
4. Integrate into `mono check` task runner

## Files to Modify

* `packages/@anthropic/mono-cli/src/tasks/bun-lock-freshness.ts` (new)
* `packages/@anthropic/mono-cli/src/commands/check.ts` (add task)
* Reference: `dotfiles/nixpkgs/home-manager/modules/direnv-stale-check/default.nix`

title: Streamline binary rebuild workflow documentation
description:
## Problem

The workflow for rebuilding stale binaries is undocumented and scattered. Users don't know the full rebuild cycle.

## Current State

* `mono nix status` - check staleness (exists)
* `mono nix rebuild` - rebuild CLIs (exists, undocumented)
* `direnv reload` - reload shell with new binaries (manual step)
* No single source of truth for the workflow

## Technical Details

Full rebuild workflow:

```bash
# 1. Check what's stale
mono nix status

# 2. Rebuild stale CLIs
mono nix rebuild

# 3. Reload shell to pick up new binaries
direnv reload
# or: exit and re-enter directory
```

The workflow is non-obvious because:

* `rebuild` updates Nix store but shell has old PATH
* Users expect rebuild to "just work" without reload
* No feedback about needing to reload

## Proposed Solution

1. **Consolidate docs**: Add "Binary Management" section to [AGENTS.md](<http://AGENTS.md>)
2. **Improve UX**: After rebuild, print reminder to reload shell
3. **Consider automation**: `mono nix rebuild --reload` that triggers direnv

## Documentation to Add

```markdown
## Binary Management

Check if CLIs need rebuilding:
```bash
mono nix status
```

Rebuild stale CLIs:

```bash
mono nix rebuild && direnv reload
```

```

## Related Issues
- oep-2dh2y1: Discoverability (complementary)
```

description:
## Problem

The `mono` CLI lacks fish shell autocompletions, making it harder to discover and use commands efficiently.

## Current State

* `mono`, `genie`, and `dotdot` CLIs all support `--completions fish` flag
* Running `mono --completions fish` outputs valid fish completion script
* Completions are not installed by default in the devenv shell

## Technical Details

The CLIs use a common completion generation pattern:

```bash
mono --completions fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/mono.fish
genie --completions fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/genie.fish
dotdot --completions fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/dotdot.fish
```

## Proposed Solution

1. Add completion generation to the Nix build for each CLI
2. Use `pkgs.runCommand` pattern (like bd completions in fish.nix)
3. Install completions to appropriate location via home-manager

## Example Implementation

```nix
monoFishCompletions = pkgs.runCommand "mono-fish-completions" { } ''
  ${mono}/bin/mono --completions fish > $out
'';
```

## Related Issues

* oep-f8jtec: Devenv-local completion loading (complementary approach)

description:
The Effect Language Service plugin emits warnings (TS28, TS36, TS41, TS43, TS44) across the codebase that cause tsc --build to exit non-zero. This blocks the pre-commit hook (check:quick -> ts:check) and CI type-check jobs.

~80 warnings total across packages, tests, and scripts. Major categories:
- preferSchemaOverJson (TS44): ~25 - JSON.parse/stringify in Effect code
- anyUnknownInErrorContext (TS28): ~30 - mostly in sync-s2/http-client-generated.ts (generated)
- globalErrorInEffectCatch (TS36): 3 - global Error in Effect.try catch
- effectFnOpportunity (TS41): ~15 - info-level suggestions
- schemaSyncInEffect (TS43): ~6 - Schema.*Sync in generators

Zero actual TS errors (error TS) - only plugin warnings/messages.
close_reason: Fixed by using Nix-provided unpatched tsc via tscBin in devenv.nix. ts:check and check:quick both pass.

comments.author: Johannes Schickling
comments.text: Starting fix: using proper Schema definitions for JSON parsing (preferSchemaOverJson) and tagged errors for catch callbacks (globalErrorInEffectCatch). 8 warnings across 4 files in scripts/src/.

comments.author: Johannes Schickling
comments.text: Commit 7f3d48767: Fixed all 8 Effect Language Service warnings in scripts/src/ — proper Schema definitions for JSON parsing, tagged errors for catch callbacks. mono ts and mono lint pass clean.

comments.author: Johannes Schickling
comments.text: CI run 21867381912 results: type-check, lint, test-unit, examples, perf, playwright, node-sync all passing. TS warnings fix in 7f3d48767 will be validated in next run. Remaining failures (wa-sqlite-test, build-deploy-docs, s2 sync) are pre-existing/unrelated.

title: Remove execIfModified workaround after devenv#2423 lands
description:
## Context

Commit f8ae0e9a4 added `lib.mkForce []` overrides in `devenv.nix` for `lint:check:format` and `lint:check:oxlint` to work around devenv-tasks' glob crate traversing node_modules (~243k files vs ~800 source files, adding ~10min overhead per task).

## TODO

Once https://github.com/cachix/devenv/pull/2423 lands and we bump the devenv input:
1. Remove the two `lib.mkForce []` overrides from `devenv.nix` (lines with the TODO comment)
2. Verify that `execIfModified` patterns work correctly without traversing node_modules
3. Confirm `dt check:quick` still completes in reasonable time (~90s or less)
